name: build_calculator_longhorizon
description: Long-horizon: build a Calculator class over three sequential prompts (arithmetic, then guarded division, then a memory), graded on the full final behavior
prompts: Create calc.py with a class Calculator. Add two methods: add(a, b) returning a + b, and sub(a, b) returning a - b.
In calc.py, add two more methods to Calculator: mul(a, b) returning a * b, and div(a, b) returning a / b, but raising ValueError when b is 0.
In calc.py, give Calculator a running memory: store(x) saves a value, recall() returns the last stored value (or 0 if nothing has been stored yet), and clear() resets the memory to 0.

test_setup_files.test_calc.py:
from calc import Calculator

c = Calculator()
assert c.add(2, 3) == 5
assert c.sub(5, 2) == 3
assert c.mul(4, 3) == 12
assert c.div(10, 2) == 5
try:
    c.div(1, 0)
    raise AssertionError("div by zero must raise ValueError")
except ValueError:
    pass
assert c.recall() == 0, "empty memory should recall 0"
c.store(42)
assert c.recall() == 42
c.clear()
assert c.recall() == 0
print("PASS")
